claims.text: The starting material is a W-Cu composite containing W particles or interconnected W ligaments in a Cu matrix.
The proposed intervention combines high-energy ball milling with subsequent spark plasma sintering.
Ball milling is proposed at 300 rpm for 10 hours.
SPS is proposed at 800 degrees Celsius and 50 MPa with a 30-minute hold.
The combined treatment will produce a homogeneous distribution of W particles in the Cu matrix.
The combined treatment will produce clean and intimate W-Cu interfaces.
High-energy ball milling breaks down the W particles.
High-energy ball milling introduces defects into the material.
Particle breakdown and milling-induced defects facilitate homogeneous W distribution during SPS.
Optimized SPS conditions remove interfacial voids.
Optimized SPS conditions form clean W-Cu interfaces.
Removal of interfacial voids and formation of clean interfaces improve thermal conductivity.
The processed composite will have at least 20% higher thermal conductivity than the untreated W-Cu composite.
The predicted conductivity improvement will persist under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions relevant to W-based plasma-facing material/Cu-based cooling-component joints.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis provides a fixed SPS recipe of 800 degrees Celsius, 50 MPa, and 30 minutes while also stating that the optimized SPS conditions remain to be determined through a systematic study.
